description: US-26 A household never pays more than the Maximalpreis — an optional, configurable upper limit on what one household pays for one distribution. FD charges 2,00 € per grown-up and 1,00 € per child, so the software quotes 11,00 € for a household of 4 grown-ups and 3 children; FD collects 5,00 €, because a Maximalpreis of 5,00 € exists that the software knows nothing about. The behavioural change is one line: priceFor returns min(per-head sum, priceCap) when a cap is configured, and every screen and use case that shows a price already reaches it through that one function. Everything else in this batch is the consequence of the value having to be configurable, versioned and auditable like every other policy value (US-14): a nullable settings column, a form field, a history diff case, an audit field, a seed. The cap is Cents | null — an EMPTY field means no cap, which is NOT the same claim as a cap of 0,00 € (free for everyone), and both must be storable and distinguishable on screen. Layered vertical slice in SEVEN stories: the domain field and the capped derivation together (adding a required field to Settings breaks every createSettings call site at once, so it is paid for once), then the diff and audit naming, then schema and repository, then the settings screen with its history, then two e2e stories, then the documents. SCHEMA CHANGE: SettingsVersion gains priceCapCents Int? (nullable); migration history is REGENERATED, not stacked on, and the hand-written partial unique index on Customer.customerNumber must be re-added. NO new port method. Source: tasks/prd-us-26-price-cap.md

userStories.title: The cap exists and priceFor honours it (domain)
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want a large household's price to stop at the Maximalpreis, so the number on screen is the number I take at the counter — which needs the value to exist on Settings first. Source: tasks/prd-us-26-price-cap.md §US-26.1 and §US-26.2
acceptanceCriteria: Settings in src/domain/policy/settings.ts gains readonly priceCap: Cents | null, placed after pricePerChild

Cents | null, NOT Cents | undefined and NOT a 0 sentinel: the column it will live in is nullable and returns null, and 0 already means something else on this screen (a child price of 0 is free, a portions count of 0 is none). One spelling end to end

createSettings validates it: null passes unconditionally; a number goes through the existing requireInteger helper with a minimum of 0 and is refused as InvalidSettings('priceCap', …) otherwise. Do NOT add a second validation helper — requireInteger already says exactly this
Do NOT add any cross-field rule. A cap BELOW pricePerGrownUp is unusual but coherent (every household then pays the cap) and must save without complaint
SettingsInput needs no new exception — priceCap is spelled the same on the form side and the domain side, unlike weekAnchor
The doc comment on the field states WHY it is nullable rather than 0-flagged, so the next reader does not 'simplify' it away

EVERY existing createSettings call site is updated so the build and the suite stay green: src/infrastructure/prisma/settings-repository.ts and src/infrastructure/prisma/seed.ts pass priceCap: null FOR NOW (US-003 replaces both), src/app/einstellungen/actions.ts passes null FOR NOW (US-004 replaces it), and every hand-written fake settings repository / settings builder under src/application/**/*.test.ts and src/domain/**/*.test.ts gains the field
STRICT TDD: the invariant-breaking test is written FIRST, red before green. One named test per rule, named after the rule rather than the function

Named tests exist for: a cap of 500 is accepted; null is accepted and means no cap; 0 is accepted and is a legal configuration, not an absent cap; -1 is refused naming priceCap; 2.5 is refused naming priceCap; a cap below pricePerGrownUp is accepted
The module stays pure: no I/O, no Date, no import from Next.js, React or Prisma

PriceValues becomes Pick<Settings, 'pricePerGrownUp' | 'pricePerChild' | 'priceCap'> — the three values the derivation reads. It stays a Pick and does NOT become the whole of Settings: the browser-side household editor prices a household as staff type, and handing it the quota and the week anchor would say those had something to do with the answer
priceFor(settings, grownUps, children) returns the per-head sum when priceCap is null, and Math.min(sum, priceCap) otherwise. Math.max appears nowhere near this — a cap is a ceiling
The result is integer cents in every case. Both operands are validated non-negative integers, so the minimum of the two is one as well; introduce NO rounding, no Math.round, no float anywhere

src/app/kunden/[id]/page.tsx adds priceCap: settings.priceCap to the AllowanceValues object it hands the household editor — the widened Pick breaks typecheck until it does. This is the two-line wiring only; the live preview is checked in the browser by US-006
The doc comment states the rule in words (the most a household pays for one distribution) and names the FD numbers the example comes from
Named test: 'charges the per-head sum when there is no cap' — priceCap null, 4 grown-ups and 3 children at 200/100 owe 1100
Named test: 'charges the per-head sum when it stays below the cap' — 1 grown-up and 1 child at 200/100 with a cap of 500 owe 300, because the cap is never reached
Named test: 'stops at the cap for a large household' — FD's own numbers: 4 grown-ups, 3 children, 200/100, cap 500 → 500, NOT 1100. This is the case the whole PRD exists for
Named BOUNDARY test: 'charges the cap exactly when the sum equals it' — sum 500, cap 500 → 500
Named test: 'charges nothing when the cap is zero' — cap 0, any household size → 0
Named test: 'caps a single-grown-up household too' — a cap below pricePerGrownUp applies to everyone; there is no minimum-household exemption
Named test: 'caps an empty household at nothing' — 0 grown-ups and 0 children owe 0, never the cap
portionsFor is UNCHANGED. The cap caps money, not food: a household over the cap still gains portions for every additional head
Domain and application coverage stay at 100% — BOTH branches of the cap are exercised: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes

The hand-written partial unique index at the end of the generated migration SQL (Customer_customerNumber_onRegister_key) is RE-ADDED after regeneration — prisma migrate dev drops it every time. src/infrastructure/prisma/schema.test.ts greps the SQL and fails if it is missing

PrismaSettingsRepository.append writes settings.priceCap into priceCapCents

The temporary priceCap: null from US-001 is GONE from both the repository and the seed

Integration test: a version written before this column existed is not a case that can occur — the migration is regenerated, so do NOT add a backfill or a default value to the column
npm run db:reset runs clean and the settings screen reports configured values afterwards (the first symptom of schema/database drift is that screen saying nothing is configured)

SettingsVersion gained nullable priceCapCents; the init migration was regenerated (20260807065541_init) with the hand-written Customer_customerNumber_onRegister_key partial index re-added, and npm run db:reset run. append writes settings.priceCap, toDomain reads row.priceCapCents ?? null through createSettings; both FOR NOW placeholders are gone and the seed sets priceCap: 500. acceptanceCriteria: A Maximalpreis field sits in the 'Mengen und Preise' card immediately after 'Preis je Kind', built with the existing EuroField (type=text inputMode=decimal, so a German comma is what staff type), name and id both 'priceCap'

The twelve-column grid is RE-SPANNED to fit six fields: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2. It is currently 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 and full, so adding a sixth field without re-spanning breaks the row. The three money fields end up the same width as each other

src/i18n/de.ts gains settings.fields.priceCap and settings.errorFields.priceCap, both 'Maximalpreis je Ausgabe' — NOT bare 'Maximalpreis': the screen also holds per-head prices and the distinguishing fact is that this one is per household per distribution

settings.prices.hint is REWORDED to state both halves of the rule: the price is calculated per head, and the Maximalpreis is the most a household pays whatever its size. It also states that leaving the field empty means there is no Maximalpreis
NO German literal anywhere in the component — every string comes from src/i18n/de.ts

actions.ts gains an OPTIONAL euro transform beside the existing euroAmount: a value that trims to '' becomes null; anything else goes through parseEuros and is refused with de.settings.errors.notAnAmount if it is not an amount. Reuse parseEuros — do NOT write a second parser

SubmittedSettings gains priceCap, formValues reads it, and shownValue restores it on a refusal, so the §4.2d defect (a refused save rewinding every field to what the database said) does not reappear for the new field

A rejected cap marks the field: InvalidSettings('priceCap') already carries the field name and it is spelled identically on both sides, so NO INPUT_NAME entry is needed

NO checkbox and NO 'Maximalpreis aktiv' toggle beside the amount. A toggle can contradict the field (5,00 € with the toggle off) and staff would have to know which wins. The empty field IS the affordance
NO cross-field validation and NO warning when the cap sits below pricePerGrownUp

The screens that SHOW a price — /ausgabe, /kunden, /kunden/[id], /kunden/[id]/karte — are NOT touched in this story and gain no Maximalpreis marker, no struck-through uncapped figure and no tooltip.
